title: Shared Canonical Component Removal Beyond Expert Views
abstract: arXiv:2610.13819v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In clinical practice, experts often begin by converting raw inputs into a set of expert features before making a decision. While black-box models trained on raw input can outperform models trained on expert views, it remains unclear what predictive signal the raw model exploits beyond what the expert view captures. We introduce an audit framework to quantify this gap using Shared Canonical Component Removal (SCCR). Unlike standard residualization or concept erasure, SCCR selectively removes only those directions strongly shared between learned raw and expert embeddings.   Evaluations on synthetic data, coronary artery disease (CAD) detection, antidepressant treatment dropout prediction, and skin lesion classification using SkinCon annotations show that SCCR identifies the ways in which expert views are insufficient and recovers residual predictive signal while minimizing redundancy with the expert view.

translated_title: 超越专家视图的共享典型成分移除
translated_abstract: 在临床实践中，专家通常首先将原始输入转换为一组专家特征，然后再做决策。尽管在原始输入上训练的黑盒模型可以超越在专家视图上训练的模型，但目前尚不清楚原始模型在专家视图所捕捉的信息之外还利用了什么预测信号。我们引入了一个审计框架，使用共享典型成分移除（SCCR）来量化这一差距。与标准的残差化或概念擦除方法不同，SCCR 仅选择性地移除学习到的原始嵌入与专家嵌入之间强烈共享的方向。在合成数据、冠心病（CAD）检测、抗抑郁治疗脱落预测以及使用 SkinCon 标注的皮肤病变分类上的评估表明，SCCR 能够识别专家视图的不足之处，并恢复残余的预测信号，同时最小化与专家视图的冗余。
tldr: 本文提出共享典型成分移除（SCCR）审计框架，通过仅移除原始嵌入与专家嵌入之间强烈共享的方向，量化并揭示黑盒模型超越专家特征所利用的残余预测信号。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Shared Canonical Component Removal (SCCR), an audit framework that selectively removes only the directions strongly shared between raw and expert embeddings, quantifying and revealing the residual predictive signal that black-box models exploit beyond expert views.
